Ava (support): Hey Liam — saw your ticket about intermittent streaming disconnects and occasional 502s when calling the /v1/stream endpoint. Can you share a sample request_id and a quick cURL run (verbose) so we can reproduce locally? Also timezone of the failures.

Liam (customer): Thanks. One failing request_id I grabbed from our app logs: rcq_20260315_abc123. Occurred 2026-03-15T20:11:02Z. We get a fast close after a few tokens, sometimes a 502. Attached a tiny log snippet.

Ava (support): Got it. Can you run this smoke check and paste the output (redact the API key):

```
curl -v \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_API_KEY" \n  -H "X-Request-ID: rcq_20260315_abc123" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  --data '{"model":"rwd-4x","input":"hello"}' \n  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream"
```

And if you can, re-run with these additional flags to capture handshake/tls: `--trace-time --trace-ascii curl-trace.txt --no-buffer --http2 --raw` and upload the `curl-trace.txt`.

Sofia (eng-oncall): For streaming problems specifically, try `--http1.1` vs `--http2` to see if it's protocol-related. If you see `upstream reset by peer` or `EOF` in the trace, include the exact TLS lines (cipher, version). Also note if there's a proxy — proxied connections often show different behavior.

Ethan (platform): If you can include the full verbose headers we can match to the edge logs. Best to run with an explicit X-Request-ID header so we can grep the gateway logs quickly. Example add `-H \"X-Debug: true\"` so we include debug response headers from the backend.

infra-bot: deploy event detected — edge/edge-2 rolled 2026-03-15T19:58:00Z on tag release/infra-2026-03-15.

Liam (customer): Ran the commands. Attaching excerpts:

```
*   Trying 52.14.200.33:443...
* Connected to api.redwood.com (52.14.200.33) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
> POST /v1/stream HTTP/2
> Host: api.redwood.com
> authorization: Bearer REDACTED_API_KEY
> x-request-id: rcq_20260315_abc123
> content-type: application/json
> content-length: 45
< HTTP/2 502
< content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
< date: Tue, 15 Mar 2026 20:11:03 GMT
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.com left intact
{"error":{"message":"upstream error: connection closed"}}
```

Ava (support): Thanks — this is very helpful. I'm going to tag eng-runtime. @Sofia can you look for rcq_20260315_abc123 in the edge logs around 2026-03-15T20:11:03Z? Also Liam, can you try two quick variants and paste both outputs: 1) `curl --http1.1 -v ...` (same headers) 2) `curl --http2 --no-buffer -v --header 'X-Debug: true'`? Please keep the X-Request-ID the same so we can correlate.

Sofia (eng-oncall): I see an edge 502 at 2026-03-15T20:11:03Z that correlates to an upstream idle timeout on edge-2 for that request_id. Need the customer's `curl-trace.txt` full file to confirm whether the client is closing or the upstream is resetting. If the `--http1.1` run succeeds, that points to an HTTP/2 multiplexing or stream reset issue. If both fail, likely an upstream transient.

Ethan (platform): Also ask the customer to include `--max-time 60` in the curl so we can rule out client-side short timeouts. And, if they're behind a corporate proxy, try a direct network from a laptop on a cellular hotspot to rule out middleboxes.

Liam (customer): Running the two variants now. Will paste both outputs and upload the full `curl-trace.txt` to INC-7890 (I removed the key). Will also try from my phone hotspot. :thumbsup:

Ava (support): Perfect — once you upload, I'll attach to the ticket and keep @Sofia/@Ethan looped. If the trace shows `RST_STREAM` from the server, we'll escalate to runtime team immediately. Thanks!
